name: Medical Doctor
summary: Doctors find out why people are sick and treat them so they can get well.
description: Medical doctors examine patients, diagnose illnesses, prescribe treatment and perform procedures. In Nigeria they work in teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, general hospitals, private clinics, the armed forces and NGOs, and many later specialise in areas such as surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology or psychiatry. Nigerian-trained doctors also practise abroad after passing that country's licensing exams.
dayToDay: A typical day includes ward rounds, seeing patients in clinic, reading test results and discussing cases with nurses and other doctors. Some days include long hospital shifts or emergency calls.
otherRoutes: Medicine is only through a university degree (MBBS/MBChB), followed by a one-year housemanship and the National Youth Service. Specialisation is through residency training with the West African College of Physicians/Surgeons or the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria.
professionalBodies: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN)
outlook: Doctors are needed in every state of Nigeria, especially in rural areas and primary health care. The training is long and demanding, but the skills are respected and in demand worldwide.

name: Nurse
summary: Nurses care for patients day and night, give medicines and help them recover.
description: Nurses assess patients, give treatment and medicines, monitor recovery and teach families how to stay healthy. They work in hospitals, primary health centres, schools, companies, the armed forces and home-care services, and can specialise in areas such as midwifery, paediatric, mental health or theatre nursing. Nigerian nurses are also widely employed in the UK, Canada, the US and the Middle East.
dayToDay: Nurses take handover from the previous shift, check vital signs, give medication, dress wounds and update patient records. They spend much of the day talking with patients and their families.
otherRoutes: Besides the BNSc degree, you can train at a hospital-based School of Nursing or School of Midwifery for the Registered Nurse (RN) or Registered Midwife (RM) certificate, and later top up to a degree.
professionalBodies: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives (NANNM)
outlook: Nurses are in high demand in Nigeria and abroad. Many hospitals need more nurses than they have, so qualified nurses rarely struggle to find work.

name: Midwife
summary: Midwives look after women during pregnancy and help babies to be born safely.
description: Midwives give antenatal care, deliver babies, look after mothers and newborns after birth and teach families about health and nutrition. They work in hospitals, maternity homes, primary health centres and community programmes across Nigeria, and they play a big part in keeping mothers and babies safe.
dayToDay: A midwife may run an antenatal clinic in the morning, support a woman in labour in the afternoon and check on new mothers and babies before the end of the shift.
otherRoutes: A School of Midwifery offers the Registered Midwife (RM) certificate, either directly or after qualifying as a nurse. Community midwifery programmes also exist.
professionalBodies: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
outlook: Skilled midwives are badly needed, especially in rural communities, and the role is valued in Nigeria and abroad.

name: Pharmacist
summary: Pharmacists are medicine experts who make sure people get the right drugs and use them safely.
description: Pharmacists check prescriptions, give out medicines, advise patients on how to use them and watch for harmful side effects. In Nigeria they work in community pharmacies, hospitals, drug manufacturing companies, regulatory agencies such as NAFDAC, and in research and sales. Some own and run their own pharmacies.
dayToDay: A hospital or community pharmacist reviews prescriptions, counsels patients, manages stock and talks with doctors about the best treatment. In industry, a pharmacist may test the quality of medicines being produced.
otherRoutes: Pharmacists need the Pharm.D or B.Pharm degree plus internship. A related role is the Pharmacy Technician, trained through ND/certificate programmes at accredited schools of health technology.
outlook: Pharmacists are needed in hospitals, communities and the growing local drug-manufacturing industry, and the qualification is recognised in many countries after further exams.

name: Dentist
summary: Dentists look after people's teeth and gums and fix problems such as tooth decay.
description: Dentists examine, clean, fill, repair and remove teeth, treat gum disease and teach people how to care for their mouths. In Nigeria they work in teaching hospitals, government hospitals, private dental clinics and the armed forces, and some specialise in areas such as orthodontics (straightening teeth) or oral surgery.
dayToDay: A dentist sees a list of patients for check-ups, fillings, extractions or cleaning, takes X-rays and explains treatment options. Running a private clinic also means managing staff and equipment.
otherRoutes: Dental Therapy and Dental Technology are related careers available through schools of health technology and some universities.
professionalBodies: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN)
outlook: Nigeria has relatively few dentists for its population, so there is room to grow, particularly outside the big cities.

name: Physiotherapist
summary: Physiotherapists help people move well again after injury, illness or surgery.
description: Physiotherapists use exercise, massage, movement training and special equipment to help people recover from injuries, strokes, surgery and long-term conditions. They work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, sports clubs, private clinics and home-care services in Nigeria and abroad.
dayToDay: A physiotherapist assesses patients, designs exercise programmes, guides them through therapy sessions and tracks their progress over weeks or months.
professionalBodies: Medical Rehabilitation Therapists (Registration) Board of Nigeria (MRTB)
outlook: Demand is growing as more people live with stroke, diabetes and sports injuries, and physiotherapists are also sought after abroad.

name: Medical Laboratory Scientist
summary: Medical lab scientists test blood and other samples to help doctors find out what is wrong.
description: Medical laboratory scientists analyse blood, urine, tissue and other samples to detect diseases such as malaria, typhoid, HIV and diabetes, and to check that blood for transfusion is safe. They work in hospital laboratories, private diagnostic centres, public health and research institutes, and blood banks.
dayToDay: Most of the day is spent in the lab running tests, using microscopes and analysers, recording results and making sure equipment and procedures meet quality standards.
otherRoutes: Medical Laboratory Technicians and Assistants can train through certificate programmes at accredited schools of health technology.
professionalBodies: Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria (MLSCN)
outlook: Every hospital and diagnostic centre needs laboratory scientists, and the skills are also useful in research and public health.

name: Radiographer
summary: Radiographers take X-rays and scans that let doctors see inside the body.
description: Radiographers operate X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI machines to produce images used to diagnose illness and injury, and therapy radiographers help treat cancer with radiation. They work in hospitals, diagnostic centres and cancer treatment centres, with good opportunities abroad.
dayToDay: A radiographer prepares patients, positions them correctly, operates the scanning equipment safely and checks that the images are clear for the doctor.
outlook: More hospitals and private centres are adding scanning equipment, so trained radiographers are needed, and the qualification is valued abroad.

name: Optometrist
summary: Optometrists test people's eyes and prescribe glasses or contact lenses.
description: Optometrists examine eyes, test vision, prescribe glasses and contact lenses, and detect eye diseases such as glaucoma early so patients can be referred for treatment. They work in eye clinics, hospitals, optical shops and their own practices.
dayToDay: An optometrist sees patients one after another, carrying out eye tests, explaining results and advising on eye care.
otherRoutes: Dispensing Opticians, who make and fit glasses, train through ND/HND-type programmes.
professionalBodies: Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Registration Board of Nigeria (ODORBN)
outlook: Many Nigerians have never had an eye test, so there is plenty of room for optometrists, including those who start their own practices.

name: Public Health Professional
summary: Public health workers protect whole communities from disease, not just one patient at a time.
description: Public health professionals plan vaccination campaigns, track disease outbreaks, run health education and improve sanitation and nutrition. In Nigeria they work with ministries of health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), primary health care agencies, NGOs and international organisations such as WHO and UNICEF.
dayToDay: A day may involve analysing health data, visiting communities, training health workers or writing reports on a programme's progress.
otherRoutes: Community Health Extension Workers (CHEW) and Environmental Health Officers can train at schools of health technology. Many people also enter public health with a master's degree (MPH) after another health or science degree.
professionalBodies: Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria (CHPRBN)
outlook: Public health work is important for Nigeria's large and growing population, with jobs in government and the NGO sector; some roles depend on donor funding.

name: Dietitian / Nutritionist
summary: Dietitians and nutritionists teach people what to eat to stay healthy or recover from illness.
description: Dietitians plan special diets for patients with conditions such as diabetes, kidney disease or malnutrition, while nutritionists also work on community feeding, food policy and health education. They work in hospitals, NGOs, food companies, schools, sports teams and private consulting.
dayToDay: A hospital dietitian reviews patients, designs meal plans with the kitchen and doctors, and counsels families. A community nutritionist may run screening and education programmes.
skills: Knowledge of food and the body
outlook: Growing concern about both malnutrition and lifestyle diseases such as diabetes is increasing interest in this field.

name: Veterinary Doctor
summary: Vets are doctors for animals, from pets to cattle and poultry.
description: Veterinary doctors diagnose and treat sick animals, vaccinate livestock and pets, inspect meat for safety and help control diseases that pass between animals and people. In Nigeria they work in private clinics, poultry and livestock farms, government veterinary services, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies and abattoirs.
dayToDay: A vet might treat dogs and cats at a clinic in the morning and visit a poultry or cattle farm in the afternoon to check on the health of the animals.
otherRoutes: Animal Health and Production Technology is available at ND/HND level for those who want to work as veterinary technicians.
outlook: Nigeria's large livestock and poultry industry, plus growing pet ownership, keeps vets in demand.

name: Civil Engineer
summary: Civil engineers design and build roads, bridges, buildings, dams and water systems.
description: Civil engineers plan, design and supervise the construction of infrastructure such as roads, bridges, drainage, water supply and large buildings. In Nigeria they work for construction companies, consulting firms, ministries of works, state agencies and as independent consultants.
dayToDay: A civil engineer may spend the morning on design calculations and drawings in the office and the afternoon on a building site checking that work is safe and done to the right standard.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Civil Engineering Technology at a polytechnic, leading to work as a technologist; HND holders can later pursue further qualifications.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Nigeria needs a great deal of new and repaired infrastructure, so civil engineers remain in steady demand, although work can depend on government and private building budgets.

name: Mechanical Engineer
summary: Mechanical engineers design and maintain machines, engines and equipment.
description: Mechanical engineers design, build and maintain machines such as engines, generators, pumps, air-conditioning systems and factory equipment. They work in manufacturing, oil and gas, power, automotive, construction and maintenance companies.
dayToDay: A day might include designing a part on a computer, testing equipment, supervising technicians or working out why a machine has broken down.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Mechanical Engineering Technology at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest engineering fields, with work in many industries in Nigeria and abroad.

name: Electrical / Electronic Engineer
summary: Electrical engineers work with electricity, from power stations to the circuits inside your phone.
description: Electrical and electronic engineers design and maintain systems that generate, transmit and use electricity, as well as electronic devices, telecoms networks and control systems. In Nigeria they work in power companies, telecoms, manufacturing, oil and gas, renewable energy and consulting.
dayToDay: An engineer may design a wiring or control system, test equipment, supervise installation of power lines or solar systems, or troubleshoot faults.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Electrical/Electronic Engineering Technology at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Improving electricity supply, renewable energy and telecoms all need electrical engineers, in Nigeria and worldwide.

name: Chemical Engineer
summary: Chemical engineers turn raw materials into useful products like fuel, medicine, food and plastics.
description: Chemical engineers design and run the processes that turn raw materials into products such as fuels, fertilisers, cement, beverages, drugs and cosmetics. In Nigeria they work in refineries, gas plants, food and drink factories, pharmaceutical companies and environmental firms.
dayToDay: A chemical engineer may monitor a production plant, analyse data to improve efficiency, check safety and environmental standards, or design new equipment.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Chemical Engineering Technology at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Chemical engineers are needed in oil and gas, manufacturing and food processing, and the skills transfer well between industries and countries.

name: Petroleum Engineer
summary: Petroleum engineers find ways to get oil and gas out of the ground safely.
description: Petroleum engineers plan how to drill wells and produce oil and gas safely and efficiently. In Nigeria they work for oil companies, oilfield service firms, regulators and consultancies, sometimes offshore or in the Niger Delta.
dayToDay: Work may involve analysing reservoir data on a computer, planning drilling operations, or spending rotations at a rig or production site.
skills: Willingness to work in remote locations
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Petroleum Engineering Technology or related programmes at some polytechnics.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Oil and gas remains important to Nigeria's economy, but jobs can rise and fall with oil prices and the world's shift to cleaner energy, so broad engineering skills are wise.

name: Computer Engineer
summary: Computer engineers design the hardware and systems that make computers and smart devices work.
description: Computer engineers combine electronics and software to design computers, embedded systems, networks and smart devices. They work in telecoms, tech companies, banks, manufacturing and research, and many also work as software developers.
dayToDay: A computer engineer may design circuits, write low-level code for a device, test hardware or configure systems for a company.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Computer Engineering Technology at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Demand is strong as Nigeria's tech sector grows, and the skills are wanted by employers worldwide.

name: Agricultural Engineer
summary: Agricultural engineers design machines and systems that help farmers grow and process more food.
description: Agricultural engineers design and maintain farm machinery, irrigation systems, storage facilities and food-processing equipment. They work with agricultural ministries, research institutes, agro-processing companies, irrigation projects and large farms.
dayToDay: A day might involve testing a processing machine, designing an irrigation layout or advising farmers on mechanisation.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Agricultural Engineering Technology at a polytechnic or college of agriculture.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Mechanising agriculture and reducing food waste are national priorities, creating opportunities in both government and private agribusiness.

name: Biomedical Engineer
summary: Biomedical engineers design and maintain the machines used in hospitals.
description: Biomedical engineers apply engineering to medicine, designing, installing and maintaining equipment such as monitors, ventilators, dialysis machines and imaging systems, and developing devices such as prosthetic limbs. They work in hospitals, medical equipment companies and research.
dayToDay: A hospital biomedical engineer checks and repairs equipment, trains staff to use it safely and advises on buying new machines.
otherRoutes: Biomedical Engineering Technology is offered at some polytechnics at ND/HND level.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: This is a newer field in Nigeria with growing need, as hospitals rely more on equipment that must be kept working.

name: Aeronautical / Aerospace Engineer
summary: Aerospace engineers design, build and maintain aircraft, drones and spacecraft.
description: Aeronautical and aerospace engineers work on the design, testing and maintenance of aircraft, engines, drones and satellites. In Nigeria they work with airlines, maintenance organisations, the Nigerian Air Force, the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) and aviation regulators, and many work abroad.
dayToDay: An engineer may inspect aircraft, analyse test data, plan maintenance schedules or work on design calculations.
otherRoutes: Aircraft Maintenance Engineering is offered by approved training schools, including the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Zaria, leading to a licence from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Opportunities in Nigeria are limited but growing with aviation and space programmes, and the skills are valued internationally.

name: Mechatronics Engineer
summary: Mechatronics engineers build smart machines and robots that combine mechanics, electronics and computing.
description: Mechatronics engineers combine mechanical, electrical and computer engineering to build automated systems, robots and smart machines. They work in manufacturing, oil and gas, automation companies and tech start-ups.
dayToDay: A mechatronics engineer may program a controller, build and test a prototype or maintain automated production lines.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Mechatronics Engineering Technology at some polytechnics.
professionalBodies: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Automation is growing worldwide, and Nigerian industries increasingly need people who understand both machines and software.

name: Mining Engineer
summary: Mining engineers plan how to dig out minerals like gold, tin, limestone and coal safely.
description: Mining engineers plan and manage the safe extraction of solid minerals such as limestone, tin, gold, coal and barite. In Nigeria they work for mining and cement companies, quarries, consulting firms and the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and its agencies.
dayToDay: A mining engineer may survey a site, plan blasting and excavation, supervise workers and check safety and environmental controls.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Mineral and Petroleum Resources Engineering or Mining Engineering Technology at some polytechnics.
professionalBodies: Council of Nigerian Mining Engineers and Geoscientists (COMEG)
outlook: Government efforts to grow the solid minerals sector may create more roles, though the industry is still developing.

name: Software Developer
summary: Software developers write the code that makes apps, websites and computer programs work.
description: Software developers design, build, test and improve applications for phones, computers and the web. In Nigeria they work for fintech companies, banks, telecoms, start-ups, software agencies and government, and many work remotely for companies abroad or as freelancers.
dayToDay: A developer writes and reviews code, fixes bugs, discusses features with teammates and tests that everything works before release.
otherRoutes: Many developers also learn through ND/HND in Computer Science, coding bootcamps, online courses and building their own projects; a strong portfolio matters a lot in this field.
outlook: Demand for good developers is strong in Nigeria's tech and fintech sector and in remote work for international companies, though entry-level roles can be competitive.

name: Data Scientist / Data Analyst
summary: Data scientists use numbers and computers to find patterns that help people make better decisions.
description: Data analysts and scientists collect, clean and study data to answer questions, build reports and create prediction models, sometimes using artificial intelligence. They work in banks, telecoms, e-commerce, health, government and consulting, in Nigeria and remotely for overseas employers.
dayToDay: A typical day includes writing queries or code to prepare data, building charts and dashboards, and explaining findings to managers.
otherRoutes: Online certificates, bootcamps and portfolio projects are common ways in, often alongside a degree in any numerate subject.
outlook: Organisations everywhere are using more data and AI, so people who can analyse data well are in demand in Nigeria and abroad.

name: Cybersecurity Analyst
summary: Cybersecurity experts protect computers, networks and people's data from hackers.
description: Cybersecurity analysts monitor systems for attacks, find weaknesses before criminals do, respond to incidents and teach staff to stay safe online. They work in banks, fintechs, telecoms, government agencies, the security services and consulting firms.
dayToDay: An analyst watches security alerts, investigates suspicious activity, tests systems for weaknesses and writes reports on how to fix them.
otherRoutes: Recognised industry certifications and practical labs are widely used to enter and progress in the field.
outlook: As banking and government services move online, the need for cybersecurity professionals is growing quickly in Nigeria and worldwide.

name: UI/UX Designer
summary: UI/UX designers plan how apps and websites look and make them easy to use.
description: UX (user experience) designers research how people use a product and plan its flow, while UI (user interface) designers create the screens, buttons and visual style. They work in tech companies, banks, agencies and start-ups, often remotely for clients abroad.
dayToDay: A designer talks to users, sketches ideas, builds prototypes in design tools and works with developers to bring the designs to life.
otherRoutes: Many designers enter through short courses, bootcamps and a strong portfolio rather than a specific degree.
outlook: Good design is increasingly valued as more services go digital, though employers look closely at portfolios.

name: Network Engineer
summary: Network engineers keep computers and phones connected to each other and the internet.
description: Network engineers design, install and maintain the networks that connect computers, offices, data centres and mobile users. In Nigeria they work for telecoms operators, internet service providers, banks, data centres and IT firms.
dayToDay: An engineer configures routers and switches, monitors network performance, fixes outages and plans upgrades.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Computer Science or Computer Engineering Technology plus vendor certifications are common routes.
outlook: Expanding broadband and mobile networks keep network engineers in demand.

name: Product Manager
summary: Product managers decide what a tech product should do and lead the team that builds it.
description: Product managers work out what users need, decide which features to build first and coordinate designers, engineers and business teams. They work in fintechs, e-commerce companies, banks and start-ups, and many people move into the role after working in engineering, design or business.
dayToDay: A product manager meets users and teammates, writes plans for new features, looks at data on how the product is used and makes trade-off decisions.
otherRoutes: Often reached after experience in another tech role, supported by short courses.
outlook: Product management is a growing career in Nigeria's tech scene, but it is rarely a first job; experience in a related role helps.

name: IT Support Specialist
summary: IT support specialists fix computer problems and help people use technology at work.
description: IT support specialists set up computers, printers and software, solve technical problems and keep office systems running. They work in schools, hospitals, banks, government offices and IT service companies, and some run their own businesses.
dayToDay: A day is spent answering help requests, installing software, fixing hardware faults and keeping records of issues.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Computer Science, IT certifications and short professional courses are common routes; this role is a good entry point into tech.
outlook: Almost every organisation needs IT support, making it a reliable entry into the technology field.

name: AI / Machine Learning Engineer
summary: AI engineers build computer systems that can learn from data, like chatbots and image recognition.
description: Machine learning engineers design, train and deploy models that recognise patterns, understand language or make predictions. They work in tech companies, banks, research labs and start-ups, in Nigeria and remotely for companies abroad.
dayToDay: An AI engineer prepares data, trains and tests models, writes code to put them into real products and monitors how well they perform.
otherRoutes: Online courses and research projects help, but a strong grounding in mathematics and programming is essential.
outlook: AI is one of the fastest-changing fields worldwide; opportunities are growing, and people who keep learning will do best.

name: Microbiologist
summary: Microbiologists study tiny living things like bacteria, viruses and fungi.
description: Microbiologists study micro-organisms to understand disease, keep food and water safe, and develop products such as vaccines and fermented foods. They work in hospitals, food and drink companies, pharmaceutical firms, research institutes, NAFDAC and universities.
dayToDay: Most of the day is spent in the laboratory growing and testing samples, recording results and writing reports.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Science Laboratory Technology (Microbiology option) at a polytechnic.
outlook: Microbiologists are needed in health, food safety and manufacturing; postgraduate study opens more research roles.

name: Biochemist
summary: Biochemists study the chemistry that happens inside living things.
description: Biochemists study chemical processes in plants, animals and people, helping to develop medicines, test food quality and understand disease. They work in hospitals, pharmaceutical and food companies, research institutes, universities and quality-control labs.
dayToDay: A biochemist runs experiments, analyses samples with lab instruments, interprets data and writes reports or research papers.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Science Laboratory Technology (Biochemistry option) at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Nigerian Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (NSBMB)
outlook: A biochemistry degree is a good base for research, industry or further study in medicine-related fields; competition for jobs means extra skills help.

name: Geologist
summary: Geologists study rocks and the Earth to find minerals, water and oil, and to understand hazards like erosion.
description: Geologists study the Earth's rocks, soils and processes to locate oil, gas, minerals and groundwater, and to assess sites for construction and hazards such as gully erosion. They work in oil and gas, mining, water drilling, construction, government geological surveys and research.
dayToDay: A geologist may spend time in the field collecting rock samples and mapping, then return to the office or lab to analyse data and write reports.
skills: Interest in nature and the outdoors
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Geology and Mining Technology at some polytechnics.
professionalBodies: Council of Nigerian Mining Engineers and Geoscientists (COMEG)
outlook: Opportunities follow the oil, mining and water sectors; groundwater and environmental work offers steady demand.

name: Physicist / Research Scientist
summary: Physicists study how the universe works, from tiny atoms to stars, and turn discoveries into technology.
description: Physicists investigate energy, matter, light, electricity and motion, and apply this knowledge in areas such as electronics, renewable energy, medical physics and space science. In Nigeria they work in universities, research agencies, energy companies, hospitals (medical physics) and teaching.
dayToDay: A research physicist designs experiments or computer models, analyses results, reads scientific papers and writes up findings.
otherRoutes: Research careers usually need a master's degree or PhD.
outlook: Pure research jobs are limited, but physics graduates are valued in technology, energy, finance and teaching because of their problem-solving skills.

name: Statistician
summary: Statisticians collect and study numbers to answer questions about people, health and business.
description: Statisticians design surveys and experiments, analyse data and explain what the numbers mean. In Nigeria they work with the National Bureau of Statistics, ministries, banks, research institutes, health programmes and market research firms.
dayToDay: A statistician plans data collection, uses software to analyse results and prepares tables and reports for decision-makers.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Statistics at a polytechnic.
outlook: Data is used everywhere, so statisticians with computing skills have good options in government, business and international organisations.

name: Environmental Scientist
summary: Environmental scientists study pollution, climate and nature and find ways to protect the environment.
description: Environmental scientists measure air, water and soil quality, assess the impact of new projects and help organisations reduce pollution and adapt to climate change. They work with environmental agencies, oil and manufacturing companies, consultancies, NGOs and research institutes.
dayToDay: Work may include collecting samples in the field, analysing data, writing environmental impact assessments and advising clients or government.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Environmental Science or related programmes at some polytechnics.
outlook: Climate change, flooding and pollution control are rising concerns, so environmental skills are increasingly needed.

name: Meteorologist
summary: Meteorologists study the weather and climate and make forecasts.
description: Meteorologists collect and analyse weather data to make forecasts and study long-term climate. In Nigeria they work mainly with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), airports, the military, agriculture and research, and they support flood and drought warnings.
dayToDay: A meteorologist studies satellite and station data, runs forecasting models and prepares weather briefings for pilots, farmers or the public.
otherRoutes: Some meteorological training is offered through specialised institutes after a science degree or diploma.
outlook: Climate change is increasing the importance of good weather and climate information for farming, aviation and disaster planning.

name: Industrial Chemist
summary: Industrial chemists test and improve the chemicals and products we use every day.
description: Industrial chemists analyse raw materials and finished products, develop new formulations and make sure products meet quality standards. They work in paint, food, beverage, cosmetics, pharmaceutical, oil and water treatment companies, and in regulatory agencies.
dayToDay: A chemist runs tests in a quality-control lab, records results and works with production staff to fix any problems.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Science Laboratory Technology (Chemistry option) at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Institute of Chartered Chemists of Nigeria (ICCON)
outlook: Manufacturing and quality control provide steady work for chemists, and local production is a growing priority.

name: Accountant
summary: Accountants keep track of money for businesses and governments and make sure the records are correct.
description: Accountants prepare and check financial records, produce reports, manage budgets, handle tax and audit organisations to make sure their figures are true. In Nigeria they work in accounting firms, banks, companies of every kind, government ministries and as independent practitioners.
dayToDay: An accountant reviews transactions, prepares statements and reports, uses accounting software and advises managers on financial decisions.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Accountancy at a polytechnic; the ICAN and ANAN professional exams (ICAN's ATS scheme accepts students from secondary school level).
professionalBodies: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN)
Association of National Accountants of Nigeria (ANAN)
outlook: Every organisation needs accountants, and professional qualification greatly improves job prospects in Nigeria and abroad.

name: Banker
summary: Bankers help people and businesses save, borrow and manage their money.
description: Bankers work in roles such as customer service, relationship management, lending, operations, treasury and risk. In Nigeria they work in commercial banks, microfinance banks, the Central Bank of Nigeria, development banks and fintech companies.
dayToDay: A relationship manager meets customers, reviews loan requests, sells banking products and meets targets set by the bank.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Banking and Finance at a polytechnic; CIBN professional exams.
professionalBodies: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN)
outlook: Banking remains a major employer, though technology is changing many roles, so digital skills are increasingly important.

name: Economist
summary: Economists study how money, jobs and prices work in a country and advise on policies.
description: Economists analyse data on prices, jobs, trade and growth to explain how the economy works and advise government and businesses. In Nigeria they work in the Central Bank, ministries, banks, research centres, international organisations and universities.
dayToDay: An economist gathers and analyses data, builds forecasts, writes reports and presents recommendations.
otherRoutes: Many economist roles require a master's degree.
outlook: Economics graduates find roles across finance, government and research; the most specialised roles favour postgraduate study and strong data skills.

name: Actuary
summary: Actuaries use maths to measure risk for insurance and pension companies.
description: Actuaries use mathematics and statistics to work out the cost of future risks, helping insurance companies set premiums and pension funds plan for the future. In Nigeria they work in insurance companies, pension fund administrators, consulting firms and regulators, and the qualification is valued internationally.
dayToDay: An actuary builds models in spreadsheets or code, analyses data on claims and life expectancy and explains findings to managers.
otherRoutes: Qualification as a fellow involves professional actuarial exams, usually taken over several years while working.
outlook: There are few qualified actuaries in Nigeria, so the profession is respected, though the exams are long and demanding.

name: Entrepreneur / Business Owner
summary: Entrepreneurs start and run their own businesses, turning ideas into products and services.
description: Entrepreneurs spot a need, create a product or service to meet it and build a business around it, from a small shop or farm to a tech start-up or factory. In Nigeria entrepreneurs drive much of the economy through small and medium enterprises, trading, manufacturing and services.
dayToDay: An entrepreneur might deal with customers, suppliers, staff, money and marketing all in the same day, constantly solving problems.
otherRoutes: Any course or trade can lead to entrepreneurship; apprenticeship, business training programmes and mentoring are common routes. Agencies such as SMEDAN support small businesses.
outlook: Entrepreneurship is central to Nigeria's economy; many businesses fail early, so planning, learning and persistence matter a great deal.

name: Marketing Manager
summary: Marketers help businesses understand customers and convince them to buy products.
description: Marketers research customers, plan campaigns, manage brands and work out prices and promotions. In Nigeria they work in consumer goods companies, banks, telecoms, advertising agencies, start-ups and as consultants.
dayToDay: A marketing manager plans campaigns, works with designers and agencies, studies sales data and meets with sales teams or customers.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Marketing at a polytechnic; professional marketing exams.
professionalBodies: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria (NIMN)
outlook: Marketing skills are needed in every industry, and digital marketing skills are especially in demand.

name: Human Resources Manager
summary: HR managers hire staff, look after their welfare and help them grow at work.
description: Human resources professionals recruit and train staff, manage pay and benefits, handle workplace issues and make sure employment laws are followed. They work in companies, banks, government agencies, NGOs and recruitment firms.
dayToDay: An HR manager may interview candidates, run a training session, resolve a staff complaint and update company policies.
otherRoutes: CIPM professional exams.
professionalBodies: Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPM)
outlook: Every medium and large organisation needs HR professionals, and certified practitioners have an advantage.

name: Procurement & Supply Chain Manager
summary: Supply chain managers make sure goods are bought, stored and delivered at the right time and cost.
description: Procurement and supply chain professionals buy materials, choose suppliers, manage stock and plan how goods move from factories to customers. They work in manufacturing, oil and gas, retail, FMCG companies, government procurement and NGOs.
dayToDay: A supply chain manager negotiates with suppliers, tracks orders and inventory and solves delays.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Purchasing and Supply at a polytechnic; CIPSMN professional exams.
professionalBodies: Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply Management of Nigeria (CIPSMN)
outlook: Growing trade and manufacturing, including regional trade in Africa, keep supply chain skills in demand.

name: Insurance Professional
summary: Insurance professionals help people and businesses protect themselves against loss.
description: Insurance professionals work as underwriters (deciding what to insure and at what price), claims officers, brokers and agents. They work in insurance companies, brokerage firms, banks and the regulator, NAICOM.
dayToDay: An underwriter studies risks and sets terms, while a broker meets clients to find them the right cover and helps them with claims.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Insurance at a polytechnic; CIIN professional exams.
outlook: Few Nigerians are currently insured, so the industry has room to grow, especially with digital insurance products.

name: Stockbroker / Investment Analyst
summary: Stockbrokers and investment analysts help people and companies invest money wisely.
description: Investment analysts study companies and markets to recommend what to buy or sell, while stockbrokers trade shares on behalf of clients. They work in stockbroking firms, investment banks, asset managers, pension fund administrators and the Nigerian Exchange.
dayToDay: An analyst reads company reports, builds financial models and writes recommendations; a broker talks with clients and places trades.
otherRoutes: Professional exams such as those of the Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers, and international investment qualifications.
outlook: Growing interest in investing, including through apps, is expanding the field; roles can be competitive and sensitive to market conditions.

name: Tax Consultant
summary: Tax consultants help people and businesses understand and pay the right amount of tax.
description: Tax professionals prepare tax returns, advise on tax laws and help organisations plan and comply. They work in accounting and law firms, companies, federal and state tax authorities, and private practice.
dayToDay: A tax consultant reviews financial records, calculates tax, files returns and keeps up with changes to tax law.
otherRoutes: CITN professional exams, often alongside ICAN or ANAN.
professionalBodies: Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN)
outlook: Government efforts to widen the tax base and frequent changes in tax law keep tax advisers in demand.

name: Business Manager / Administrator
summary: Business managers organise people, money and plans so that companies run smoothly.
description: Business managers and administrators plan operations, supervise staff, manage budgets and make sure targets are met. They work in companies of every size, NGOs, schools, hospitals and government agencies.
dayToDay: A manager holds meetings, reviews reports, solves staff and customer problems and plans the next steps for the team.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Business Administration and Management or Office Technology and Management at a polytechnic.
outlook: Management skills are useful in almost every sector; experience and results count as much as qualifications.

name: Lawyer
summary: Lawyers advise people and organisations on the law and represent them in court.
description: Lawyers (called barristers and solicitors in Nigeria) give legal advice, draft contracts and documents, and represent clients in court. They work in law firms, companies, banks, government ministries, the Ministry of Justice, NGOs and their own practices, in areas such as corporate, criminal, family, property and human rights law.
dayToDay: A lawyer researches cases, meets clients, drafts documents, negotiates and appears in court.
otherRoutes: After the LL.B degree, graduates attend the Nigerian Law School for the Bar programme before being called to the Nigerian Bar. Paralegal certificates exist for support roles.
professionalBodies: Council of Legal Education (Nigerian Law School)
outlook: Law is a respected profession with many paths; the field is competitive, so strong writing, specialisation and experience help.

name: Judge / Magistrate
summary: Judges listen to both sides in court and decide cases fairly according to the law.
description: Judges and magistrates hear cases, weigh evidence and arguments, and deliver judgments. Becoming a judge in Nigeria usually requires many years of experience as a lawyer before appointment to a magistrate court, high court or higher court.
dayToDay: A judge presides over court sessions, reads case files and legal arguments, and writes judgments.
otherRoutes: The path is through law: LL.B, Nigerian Law School, call to the Bar, then years of practice before judicial appointment.
outlook: Judicial appointments are few and come later in a legal career, but they are among the most respected roles in public life.

name: Diplomat / Foreign Service Officer
summary: Diplomats represent Nigeria in other countries and work to build good relationships.
description: Diplomats represent Nigeria abroad, negotiate agreements, support Nigerians overseas and promote trade and culture. Most work in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Nigerian embassies and high commissions; related roles exist in the African Union, ECOWAS and the United Nations.
dayToDay: A foreign service officer writes reports on events, attends meetings with officials, handles consular services and prepares briefings.
otherRoutes: Entry is usually through competitive Foreign Service recruitment exams for graduates.
outlook: Places are limited and competitive; strong languages and knowledge of international affairs help, and similar skills are useful in international organisations.

name: Civil Servant / Public Administrator
summary: Civil servants work in government ministries and agencies to deliver public services.
description: Civil servants plan and run government programmes, manage public money, draft policies and serve citizens. They work in federal, state and local government ministries, departments and agencies across Nigeria, in roles from administration to specialist posts.
dayToDay: A civil servant may prepare memos and reports, attend meetings, process files and coordinate projects with other agencies.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Public Administration at a polytechnic. Graduates of most courses can join through public service recruitment.
outlook: Government is a major employer; recruitment varies over time, and people with specialist skills have more options.

name: Public Policy Analyst / Politician
summary: Policy analysts and politicians work on the laws and decisions that shape how a country is run.
description: Policy analysts research problems and recommend solutions to governments, while elected politicians represent citizens and make laws. Policy roles exist in think tanks, NGOs, legislatures, ministries and international organisations; politics usually builds on experience in another career and community service.
dayToDay: An analyst reads research, interviews experts and writes policy briefs; a legislator attends sittings, committee meetings and meets constituents.
otherRoutes: Many enter politics after careers in law, business, medicine or community work.
outlook: Good policy work is always needed; political careers are uncertain and depend on elections and public trust.

name: Customs Officer
summary: Customs officers check goods coming into and leaving Nigeria and collect import duties.
description: Customs officers inspect goods at ports, airports and borders, collect duties and taxes, and stop smuggling of banned items. They work for the Nigeria Customs Service in a uniformed, disciplined career with ranks.
dayToDay: An officer checks documents and cargo, uses scanning equipment, calculates duties and may take part in anti-smuggling patrols.
otherRoutes: Recruitment exercises accept applicants with SSCE, ND/HND or degrees for different entry ranks.
outlook: Recruitment happens periodically and is competitive; the job offers a structured career in public service.

name: Immigration Officer
summary: Immigration officers control who enters and leaves Nigeria and issue passports.
description: Immigration officers check travel documents at airports and borders, issue passports and residence permits, and help prevent human trafficking and illegal migration. They work for the Nigeria Immigration Service, a uniformed service with ranks.
dayToDay: An officer screens travellers, verifies documents, processes passport applications and works with other security agencies.
otherRoutes: Recruitment exercises accept applicants with SSCE, ND/HND or degrees for different entry ranks.
outlook: Recruitment is periodic and competitive, and the role offers a steady public-service career.

name: Teacher
summary: Teachers help children and young people learn and grow.
description: Teachers plan lessons, teach subjects, assess learning and support students' personal development. In Nigeria they work in nursery, primary and secondary schools, both public and private, as well as in tutorial centres, online platforms and international schools; many Nigerian teachers also teach abroad.
dayToDay: A teacher prepares and delivers lessons, marks work, supports students who are struggling and talks with parents and colleagues.
otherRoutes: The Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) at a College of Education qualifies you to teach; graduates of other subjects can take a Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE).
outlook: Good teachers are always needed, especially in science, mathematics and technical subjects, and teaching skills are portable worldwide.

name: University Lecturer
summary: Lecturers teach students at university or polytechnic and carry out research.
description: Lecturers teach undergraduate and postgraduate students, supervise projects, carry out research and publish their findings. They work in federal, state and private universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, and may also consult for government and industry.
dayToDay: A lecturer gives lectures, marks scripts, supervises student projects, works on research and attends departmental meetings.
otherRoutes: Usually requires a strong first degree, then a master's degree and often a PhD.
outlook: Higher education is expanding with new universities, creating openings for well-qualified academics, especially those with PhDs.

name: School Counsellor
summary: School counsellors help students with their studies, career choices and personal worries.
description: School counsellors guide students on subject and career choices, support them through personal or emotional difficulties and work with parents and teachers. They work in secondary schools, universities, and counselling centres.
dayToDay: A counsellor meets students one-to-one, runs career talks, gives aptitude or interest tests and keeps confidential notes.
outlook: Schools are giving more attention to student wellbeing and career guidance, increasing the value of trained counsellors.

name: Librarian
summary: Librarians organise books and information and help people find what they need.
description: Librarians manage collections of books, journals and digital resources, help users with research and run reading and information programmes. They work in school, university, public and special libraries, as well as in companies, archives and digital information services.
dayToDay: A librarian catalogues materials, helps readers find information, manages digital databases and organises reading activities.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Library and Information Science at a polytechnic.
outlook: Libraries are becoming more digital, so librarians with technology and data skills have the best prospects.

name: Journalist
summary: Journalists find out what is happening and report the news accurately.
description: Journalists research, interview people and write or produce stories for newspapers, websites, radio, TV and podcasts. In Nigeria they work for national and regional media houses, online news platforms, international news agencies and as freelancers, covering areas such as politics, business, sport, health and investigations.
dayToDay: A journalist pitches story ideas, interviews sources, checks facts, writes or records the story and meets tight deadlines.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Mass Communication at a polytechnic; short courses and building a portfolio of published work.
outlook: Traditional media is changing fast, but trustworthy reporting is still needed; digital, data and video skills improve prospects.

name: Broadcaster / Presenter
summary: Broadcasters present programmes on radio, TV and online.
description: Broadcasters host news, talk shows, sports, music and entertainment programmes on radio, television and digital platforms. In Nigeria they work for government and private stations, including stations that broadcast in Nigerian languages, and increasingly on podcasts and online channels.
dayToDay: A presenter researches topics, prepares scripts, interviews guests and goes live on air, often working early mornings or late nights.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Mass Communication; many presenters start through campus radio, internships and training at broadcasting institutes.
outlook: There are many radio and TV stations plus fast-growing online platforms, though popular roles are competitive.

name: Filmmaker (Nollywood)
summary: Filmmakers tell stories through films, series and videos.
description: Filmmakers include directors, producers, cinematographers, editors and screenwriters who create films, TV series, documentaries and adverts. Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, is one of the largest in the world, and Nigerian content now also reaches streaming platforms and audiences abroad.
dayToDay: Depending on the role, a day may involve writing scripts, planning shoots, directing actors, filming on set or editing footage.
otherRoutes: Film schools, short courses, workshops and working on sets as an assistant are common routes in.
professionalBodies: National Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB) (regulator)
outlook: Nollywood and streaming are growing, but work is often project-based, so building skills, networks and a reel is important.

name: Actor / Performer
summary: Actors bring characters to life in films, TV, theatre and adverts.
description: Actors perform roles in films, TV series, stage plays, adverts and voice-overs. In Nigeria they work in Nollywood, theatre, television and advertising, and many also present, model or create online content.
dayToDay: An actor learns lines, attends auditions and rehearsals, and spends long days on set or performing on stage.
otherRoutes: Acting workshops, drama groups, church or community theatre and auditions are common routes.
outlook: Opportunities are increasing with Nollywood and streaming, but income can be irregular, so many actors build other skills alongside acting.

name: Musician / Music Producer
summary: Musicians create and perform music, and producers help record and shape songs.
description: Musicians write, perform and record music, while producers and sound engineers arrange, record and mix songs. Nigerian music, including Afrobeats, gospel, highlife and fuji, has audiences worldwide, and musicians work as artists, session players, teachers, church and event musicians and in studios.
dayToDay: A day may include practising, writing songs, recording in a studio, rehearsing with a band or performing at events.
otherRoutes: Music schools, private lessons, church and community music groups, and studio apprenticeships are common routes.
professionalBodies: Performing Musicians Employers' Association of Nigeria (PMAN)
outlook: The global popularity of Nigerian music creates real opportunities, but success is uncertain; business, digital and production skills help a lot.

name: Graphic Designer
summary: Graphic designers create logos, posters, adverts and images that communicate ideas.
description: Graphic designers combine images, colour and text to create logos, brand identities, packaging, adverts, social media graphics and publications. They work in advertising agencies, media houses, companies, printing firms and as freelancers for local and international clients.
dayToDay: A designer meets clients to understand a brief, sketches ideas, creates designs on the computer and revises them based on feedback.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Art and Design at a polytechnic; short courses and a strong portfolio.
outlook: Businesses of all sizes need design for digital and print, and skilled designers can also work remotely for clients abroad.

name: Fashion Designer
summary: Fashion designers create clothes, shoes and accessories and build fashion brands.
description: Fashion designers sketch, choose fabrics and create clothing and accessories, from traditional attire to ready-to-wear and bridal wear. In Nigeria many run their own labels and studios, while others work for fashion houses, film and stage productions, and retailers; Nigerian fashion is increasingly recognised abroad.
dayToDay: A designer sketches new ideas, meets clients, selects fabrics, supervises tailors and markets the brand online.
otherRoutes: Fashion schools, apprenticeship with an established designer and ND/HND in Fashion Design and Clothing Technology.
outlook: Fashion is a major creative industry in Nigeria with export potential, though building a brand takes time and business skills.

name: Photographer / Videographer
summary: Photographers capture images and videos for events, news, adverts and art.
description: Photographers and videographers take and edit pictures and videos for weddings and events, news, fashion, products, real estate and social media. Most in Nigeria are self-employed or run studios, while others work for media houses and agencies.
dayToDay: A photographer plans shoots, sets up lighting and equipment, takes pictures or video and spends time editing and delivering to clients.
otherRoutes: Apprenticeship with a professional photographer, short courses and building a portfolio.
outlook: Demand for events, social media and product photography is high, but competition is strong, so quality and reputation matter.

name: Digital Marketer / Content Creator
summary: Digital marketers and content creators make posts and videos online and help brands reach customers.
description: Digital marketers plan and run online campaigns using social media, search engines, email and websites, while content creators produce videos, posts and podcasts that build an audience. They work for brands, agencies, media companies and start-ups, or for themselves.
dayToDay: A day may include planning content, filming or writing posts, checking analytics to see what works and talking with clients or brands.
otherRoutes: Online certifications, short courses and a portfolio of real campaigns or content are the most common routes.
professionalBodies: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria (NIMN)
outlook: Businesses are moving their marketing online, so skilled digital marketers are in demand; full-time content creation is possible but uncertain.

name: Writer / Author
summary: Writers create books, stories, scripts and articles that inform and entertain people.
description: Writers produce novels, poems, plays, screenplays, children's books, speeches and copy for adverts and websites. Nigeria has a strong literary tradition, and writers work as authors, copywriters, editors, scriptwriters, speechwriters and content writers, often combining several of these.
dayToDay: A writer researches, drafts, revises and edits, often working with editors, publishers or clients.
otherRoutes: Writing workshops, competitions and publishing work online are common ways to start.
outlook: Earning a living from books alone is hard, but writing skills are valued in media, marketing, film and business.

name: Architect
summary: Architects design buildings that are safe, useful and beautiful.
description: Architects design houses, schools, hospitals, offices and public spaces, and oversee construction to make sure the design is followed. In Nigeria they work in architectural firms, construction and real estate companies, government planning and works departments, and their own practices.
dayToDay: An architect meets clients, sketches and develops designs with software, prepares drawings, coordinates with engineers and visits sites.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Architectural Technology at a polytechnic leads to work as an architectural technologist.
outlook: Rapid urban growth means buildings are needed everywhere; the training is long, and registration is required to practise as an architect.

name: Quantity Surveyor
summary: Quantity surveyors work out how much a building project will cost and keep spending under control.
description: Quantity surveyors estimate and manage the costs of construction projects, prepare bills of quantities, advise on contracts and value completed work. They work in consulting firms, construction companies, banks, government agencies and oil and gas projects.
dayToDay: A quantity surveyor measures from drawings, prices materials and labour, visits sites to value work and prepares cost reports.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Quantity Surveying at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria (QSRBN)
outlook: Construction and infrastructure projects need cost control, so registered quantity surveyors are steadily in demand.

name: Estate Surveyor and Valuer
summary: Estate surveyors value, sell, let and manage land and buildings.
description: Estate surveyors and valuers determine the value of property, manage estates, advise on buying and selling, and handle rentals. They work in real estate firms, banks, insurance companies, government lands departments and their own practices.
dayToDay: An estate surveyor inspects properties, prepares valuation reports, meets clients and tenants and negotiates deals.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Estate Management at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Estate Surveyors and Valuers Registration Board of Nigeria (ESVARBON)
Nigerian Institution of Estate Surveyors and Valuers (NIESV)
outlook: Growing cities and the real estate market create demand, and registration is needed to practise as a valuer.

name: Urban and Regional Planner
summary: Town planners decide how land in cities and towns should be used so that communities work well.
description: Urban and regional planners plan the layout of towns and cities, decide where roads, homes, markets, schools and parks should go, and review building approvals. They work in state and local planning authorities, development agencies, consultancies and NGOs.
dayToDay: A planner studies maps and data, visits sites, reviews building applications and consults communities on development plans.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Urban and Regional Planning at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Town Planners Registration Council of Nigeria (TOPREC)
outlook: Nigeria's fast-growing cities need good planning to tackle flooding, traffic and housing, so planners have an important role.

name: Builder / Building Technologist
summary: Builders manage construction sites and turn building designs into real structures.
description: Builders and building technologists plan and manage construction work, organise workers and materials, and make sure buildings meet safety and quality standards. They work for construction companies, developers, government agencies and as contractors.
dayToDay: A builder supervises site work, checks quality, orders materials, keeps the project on schedule and enforces safety.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Building Technology at a polytechnic; trade training in masonry and other building crafts.
professionalBodies: Council of Registered Builders of Nigeria (CORBON)
outlook: Housing and infrastructure needs are large, so building professionals are needed, especially to improve safety on sites.

name: Land Surveyor
summary: Surveyors measure land accurately and make maps used for building, roads and property titles.
description: Land surveyors measure and map land, mark property boundaries and provide data for construction, roads, mining and land registration. They work in surveying firms, construction and oil companies, government survey departments and their own practices, increasingly using GPS, drones and GIS.
dayToDay: A surveyor works in the field with surveying instruments, then processes the measurements and produces plans and maps in the office.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Surveying and Geoinformatics at a polytechnic.
outlook: Land titling, construction and mapping keep surveyors busy, and digital mapping skills are increasingly valuable.

name: Agronomist / Farm Manager
summary: Agronomists and farm managers help crops grow well and run farms as successful businesses.
description: Agronomists study soil and crops and advise farmers on seeds, fertiliser, pests and irrigation, while farm managers run day-to-day farm operations. They work on commercial farms, with seed and fertiliser companies, agricultural development programmes, research institutes and on their own farms.
dayToDay: A farm manager plans planting and harvesting, supervises workers, checks crops for pests and disease and keeps farm records.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Agricultural Technology at a polytechnic or college of agriculture; farm apprenticeship and extension training programmes.
outlook: Food security is a national priority and modern, mechanised farming is growing, creating opportunities for skilled agricultural professionals.

name: Agribusiness Manager
summary: Agribusiness managers turn farming into business by processing, packaging and selling farm products.
description: Agribusiness professionals manage the business side of agriculture, from buying inputs and financing farmers to processing, packaging, transporting and exporting farm produce. They work in agro-processing companies, agricultural banks and fintechs, cooperatives, NGOs and their own businesses.
dayToDay: An agribusiness manager might negotiate with farmers, plan logistics, manage a processing plant or look for new markets.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Agricultural Technology or Business Administration; agribusiness training and start-up programmes.
outlook: Adding value to farm produce is a big opportunity in Nigeria, with growing interest from investors and young entrepreneurs.

name: Fisheries and Aquaculture Specialist
summary: Fisheries specialists raise fish in ponds and help manage fish in rivers and the sea.
description: Fisheries and aquaculture specialists breed and raise fish such as catfish and tilapia, manage fish farms and hatcheries, and help protect wild fish stocks. They work on fish farms, with feed companies, in government fisheries departments, research institutes and their own businesses.
dayToDay: An aquaculture manager checks water quality, feeds and monitors fish, controls disease and arranges sales.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Fisheries Technology at a polytechnic or college of agriculture; practical training on fish farms.
outlook: Nigeria produces less fish than it consumes, so fish farming is a real business opportunity.

name: Forestry and Wildlife Officer
summary: Forestry officers look after forests, trees and wild animals.
description: Forestry and wildlife professionals manage forests and national parks, plant trees, protect wildlife and work on sustainable timber and conservation. They work with forestry departments, the National Park Service, conservation NGOs, research institutes and timber companies.
dayToDay: An officer may patrol a forest reserve, survey trees or animals, supervise tree planting and work with local communities.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Forestry Technology at a college of forestry or polytechnic.
outlook: Deforestation and climate change make conservation and tree-planting work increasingly important.

name: Food Scientist / Technologist
summary: Food scientists make sure the food we eat is safe, healthy and tasty.
description: Food scientists and technologists develop new food products, improve processing and packaging and test food for safety and quality. They work in food and beverage companies, NAFDAC and other regulators, research institutes and agro-processing businesses.
dayToDay: A food technologist runs quality tests, monitors production lines, develops recipes for new products and keeps hygiene records.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Food Technology at a polytechnic.
professionalBodies: Nigerian Institute of Food Science and Technology (NIFST)
outlook: Nigeria's large food and drink industry and drive to process local produce keep food scientists in demand.

name: Electrician
summary: Electricians install and repair wiring, sockets, lights and electrical equipment safely.
description: Electricians install, maintain and repair electrical wiring and equipment in homes, offices, factories and construction sites. Many in Nigeria are self-employed contractors, while others work for construction firms, factories, estates and power companies.
dayToDay: An electrician reads drawings, runs cables, installs fittings, tests circuits and finds and fixes faults.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
professionalBodies: Nigerian Electricity Management Services Agency (NEMSA) (certification of electrical installers)
outlook: Electricians are needed everywhere, from new buildings to solar and backup power, and skilled, reliable electricians rarely lack work.

name: Plumber
summary: Plumbers install and fix water pipes, taps, toilets and drainage.
description: Plumbers install and repair water supply, drainage and sanitation systems in homes, offices, hotels and factories. Most work as independent tradespeople or for construction and facility management companies.
dayToDay: A plumber visits sites to install pipes and fittings, fix leaks and blockages, and give customers quotes.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
outlook: Building and maintenance work keep good plumbers in steady demand, and many build their own businesses.

name: Auto Mechanic / Automotive Technician
summary: Auto mechanics find and fix problems with cars, buses and motorcycles.
description: Automotive technicians service and repair vehicles, from engines and brakes to electrical and computer systems. They work in workshops, car dealerships, transport companies and their own garages.
dayToDay: A mechanic diagnoses faults, often using computer scanners, replaces parts, services vehicles and explains repairs to customers.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
outlook: Vehicles are everywhere in Nigeria, and mechanics who can work on modern, computer-controlled and electric vehicles will be most in demand.

name: Welder / Fabricator
summary: Welders join metal parts together to make gates, structures, pipelines and machines.
description: Welders and fabricators cut, shape and join metal to build gates, roofs, tanks, pipelines, ships and machine parts. They work in fabrication workshops, construction, oil and gas, shipbuilding and their own businesses; certified welders can also work abroad.
dayToDay: A welder reads drawings, measures and cuts metal, welds pieces together safely and checks the quality of the joints.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics. Internationally recognised welding certifications open higher-paying industrial work.
outlook: Construction, manufacturing and oil and gas all need skilled welders, and certified welders are in demand at home and abroad.

name: Carpenter / Furniture Maker
summary: Carpenters make furniture, doors, roofs and other things from wood.
description: Carpenters and furniture makers design and build furniture, cabinets, doors, roofs and fittings. Many in Nigeria run their own workshops, while others work for construction and interior design companies.
dayToDay: A carpenter measures, cuts and joins wood, uses hand and power tools, finishes products and meets customers.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
outlook: Quality, well-designed furniture is in demand, and skilled makers can grow strong local brands.

name: Tailor / Garment Maker
summary: Tailors measure, cut and sew clothes that fit people well.
description: Tailors and garment makers make and alter clothes, from native attire and uniforms to suits and dresses. Many work for themselves, while others work for fashion houses, uniform makers and garment factories.
dayToDay: A tailor takes measurements, cuts fabric, sews garments, fits them on clients and meets delivery dates.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
outlook: Made-to-measure clothing is a big part of Nigerian life, so skilled, reliable tailors always find customers.

name: Hairdresser / Cosmetologist
summary: Hairdressers and cosmetologists style hair and help people look and feel their best.
description: Hair stylists, barbers, make-up artists and beauty therapists cut, braid and style hair, apply make-up and offer skin and nail care. Most run their own salons or work in salons, spas, film and TV productions and events.
dayToDay: A stylist attends to clients, recommends styles and products, keeps tools hygienic and promotes their work online.
otherRoutes: Apprenticeship in a salon, beauty and cosmetology schools and short certificate courses.
outlook: The beauty industry is large and growing, and skilled stylists with good customer service build loyal clients.

name: Solar Installer / Renewable Energy Technician
summary: Solar installers set up solar panels and batteries so homes and businesses have power.
description: Solar and renewable energy technicians design, install and maintain solar panels, inverters and batteries for homes, businesses, schools and health centres. They work for solar companies, mini-grid developers and as independent installers.
dayToDay: A technician assesses a building's power needs, mounts panels, wires inverters and batteries, tests the system and fixes faults.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics. Specialised solar installation training and certificates are offered by several institutions and private providers.
professionalBodies: Nigerian Electricity Management Services Agency (NEMSA) (certification of electrical installers)
outlook: Solar power is growing quickly in Nigeria because of unreliable grid supply, so trained installers are in strong demand.

name: Phone and Electronics Repairer
summary: Electronics repairers fix phones, laptops, TVs and other gadgets.
description: Phone and electronics technicians diagnose and repair phones, computers, televisions and other devices, replacing screens, batteries and circuit components. Most run their own shops, while others work for repair centres and device retailers.
dayToDay: A repairer tests faulty devices, replaces parts, solders components, installs software and advises customers.
otherRoutes: Formal apprenticeship with a skilled master craftsperson, trade tests and certificates (for example NABTEB examinations or programmes supported by the Industrial Training Fund), technical colleges, and ND/HND at polytechnics.
outlook: With so many phones and devices in use, repair skills are always needed, and quality, trustworthy repairers do well.

name: Chef / Caterer
summary: Chefs and caterers cook delicious meals for restaurants, hotels and events.
description: Chefs plan menus and prepare food in restaurants, hotels and institutions, while caterers cook for weddings, parties and corporate events. Many Nigerian chefs run their own catering businesses, bakeries or food brands.
dayToDay: A chef plans menus, buys ingredients, cooks and supervises kitchen staff, and keeps the kitchen clean and safe.
otherRoutes: Culinary schools, apprenticeship in a kitchen, and ND/HND in Hospitality Management at a polytechnic.
outlook: Food businesses are popular and growing, and skilled chefs can work in Nigeria, on cruise ships or abroad.

name: Hotel Manager
summary: Hotel managers make sure guests are comfortable and that the hotel runs smoothly.
description: Hotel managers oversee rooms, food and drinks, events, staff and finances in hotels, resorts and guest houses. They work for local and international hotel brands and serviced apartments, or run their own establishments.
dayToDay: A hotel manager checks on departments, handles guest feedback, plans staff rotas, reviews finances and maintains standards.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Hospitality Management at a polytechnic; training at the National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism (NIHOTOUR); working up from front office or restaurant roles.
outlook: Hospitality grows with business travel and tourism, and experience in good hotels is valued internationally.

name: Travel Consultant / Tour Guide
summary: Travel consultants plan trips for people and tour guides show visitors interesting places.
description: Travel consultants book flights, hotels and tours, and advise on visas and travel plans, while tour guides lead visitors around cultural, historical and natural sites. They work for travel agencies, tour operators, airlines, tourism boards and their own businesses.
dayToDay: A travel consultant talks with clients, searches booking systems and arranges itineraries; a tour guide leads groups and tells the stories of each place.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Leisure and Tourism Management; NIHOTOUR courses; airline ticketing and travel-agency certificates.
professionalBodies: National Association of Nigerian Travel Agencies (NANTA)
outlook: Travel and domestic tourism are growing, though they can be affected by the economy and security; online skills are increasingly important.

name: Event Planner
summary: Event planners organise weddings, conferences, parties and concerts so everything runs perfectly.
description: Event planners plan and coordinate weddings, birthdays, conferences, product launches and concerts, managing budgets, venues, vendors and guests. Most in Nigeria run their own businesses, while others work for hotels, agencies and corporate organisations.
dayToDay: An event planner meets clients, negotiates with vendors, plans schedules and is on site to manage everything on the day.
