otherRoutes: Working as an assistant to an established planner, short courses and building a portfolio of events.
outlook: Nigerians love celebrations, and events are a big industry; success depends on reputation and referrals.

name: Airline Pilot
summary: Pilots fly aeroplanes and helicopters safely, carrying passengers and cargo.
description: Pilots plan flights, operate aircraft and keep passengers and crew safe. In Nigeria they fly for domestic and international airlines, private and charter operators, helicopter companies serving the oil industry, and the Nigerian Air Force.
dayToDay: A pilot checks weather and flight plans, inspects the aircraft, flies the route with the co-pilot and communicates with air traffic control.
otherRoutes: Pilot training is through approved flying schools such as the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Zaria, or abroad, leading to licences issued by the NCAA. A degree is helpful but not always required. The Nigerian Air Force trains its own pilots.
outlook: Pilots are needed worldwide as air travel grows; training is expensive and demanding, so scholarships and sponsorship schemes are worth exploring.

name: Cabin Crew / Flight Attendant
summary: Cabin crew keep passengers safe and comfortable on flights.
description: Cabin crew carry out safety checks, give safety briefings, serve passengers and handle emergencies on board. They work for domestic and international airlines and private jet operators.
dayToDay: Crew attend a pre-flight briefing, check safety equipment, welcome passengers, serve meals and handle any problems during the flight.
otherRoutes: Airlines recruit and train cabin crew, and approved aviation schools offer cabin crew certificates recognised by the NCAA.
outlook: Opportunities follow the growth of airlines; the job involves irregular hours but offers travel and transferable customer-service skills.

name: Marine Engineer / Seafarer
summary: Seafarers and marine engineers run and navigate ships that carry goods across the seas.
description: Marine engineers maintain ships' engines and machinery, while deck officers navigate and command vessels. They work on cargo ships, oil tankers, offshore vessels and ports, in Nigeria and worldwide.
dayToDay: At sea, a marine engineer works watches in the engine room, maintaining machinery; a deck officer keeps navigation watches and manages cargo.
skills: Ability to spend long periods at sea
otherRoutes: Training at the Maritime Academy of Nigeria, Oron, and other approved institutions, with sea time and certificates of competency issued through NIMASA.
professionalBodies: Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA)
Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN)
outlook: Global shipping needs certified seafarers; getting the required sea time can be the hardest step, so look for cadet programmes.

name: Logistics Manager
summary: Logistics managers organise how goods are moved and delivered on time.
description: Logistics managers plan the movement and storage of goods by road, rail, sea and air, manage warehouses and delivery fleets, and handle shipping and customs paperwork. They work for logistics and courier companies, e-commerce firms, manufacturers, ports and shipping lines.
dayToDay: A logistics manager plans routes, tracks shipments, manages drivers and warehouse staff, and solves delays.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Transport Management or Purchasing and Supply; professional exams in logistics and transport.
professionalBodies: Chartered Institute of Logistics and Transport (CILT) Nigeria
Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply Management of Nigeria (CIPSMN)
outlook: E-commerce and trade growth are increasing demand for logistics professionals.

name: Military Officer
summary: Military officers lead soldiers, sailors or air force personnel to defend the country.
description: Military officers lead and manage personnel in the Nigerian Army, Navy and Air Force, plan operations and support peacekeeping and disaster relief. Officers can also specialise as engineers, doctors, pilots, lawyers or in logistics.
dayToDay: An officer leads training, plans and supervises operations, manages equipment and looks after the welfare of the people under their command.
otherRoutes: Entry as a cadet through the Nigerian Defence Academy, Kaduna, after secondary school, or as a graduate through short service or direct commission. Non-commissioned roles are open through regular recruitment.
outlook: The armed forces recruit regularly; the career offers structure and training but involves risk and postings anywhere in the country.

name: Police Officer
summary: Police officers protect people, prevent crime and enforce the law.
description: Police officers keep public order, investigate crimes, respond to emergencies and work with communities to keep them safe. In Nigeria they serve in the Nigeria Police Force in roles such as patrol, investigation, intelligence, cybercrime and forensics.
dayToDay: An officer may patrol an area, respond to calls, take statements, investigate cases and prepare reports for court.
otherRoutes: The Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, offers degree programmes for cadets; recruitment also takes place at constable, inspector and graduate levels.
outlook: Policing is always needed; officers with investigation, forensic and digital skills are increasingly valuable.

name: Firefighter
summary: Firefighters put out fires, rescue people and teach communities about fire safety.
description: Firefighters respond to fires, road accidents, building collapses and other emergencies, and carry out fire-safety inspections and education. In Nigeria they work in the Federal Fire Service, state fire services, airports, oil and gas facilities and large companies.
dayToDay: A firefighter checks equipment, trains and keeps fit, responds to emergency calls and visits buildings for safety inspections.
otherRoutes: Recruitment into fire services with training at fire service training schools; health, safety and environment certificates support industrial roles.
outlook: Fire and emergency services need more trained personnel as cities and industries grow.

name: Social Worker
summary: Social workers help children, families and vulnerable people through difficult times.
description: Social workers support people facing problems such as poverty, abuse, disability, illness or family breakdown, connecting them with help and protecting vulnerable children and adults. In Nigeria they work in hospitals, ministries of women affairs and social development, courts, NGOs, schools and international agencies.
dayToDay: A social worker visits families, assesses needs, writes case reports, links people to services and may attend court for child protection cases.
otherRoutes: ND/HND in Social Development at a polytechnic.
outlook: Social workers are needed in health, child protection and humanitarian work, especially with NGOs and international agencies.

name: Psychologist
summary: Psychologists study how people think, feel and behave and help them with their mental health.
description: Psychologists assess and support people with emotional, behavioural and mental health difficulties, and also work in areas such as education, organisations and research. In Nigeria they work in hospitals, schools, companies, prisons and correctional centres, NGOs, the military and private practice.
dayToDay: A clinical psychologist meets clients for therapy sessions, carries out assessments and writes reports; an organisational psychologist might design staff selection tests.
otherRoutes: Clinical practice usually requires postgraduate training after the first degree.
outlook: Awareness of mental health is growing in Nigeria, and there are too few trained psychologists for the need.

name: Religious Leader / Chaplain
summary: Religious leaders guide and support their faith communities.
description: Religious leaders such as pastors, priests, imams and chaplains lead worship, teach, counsel members of their communities and organise charitable work. They work in churches and mosques, schools, hospitals, the armed forces, prisons and faith-based organisations, according to the requirements of their own faith tradition.
dayToDay: A day may include leading prayers or services, teaching, counselling individuals or families, visiting the sick and coordinating community activities.
otherRoutes: Seminaries, theological colleges and Islamic institutions train religious leaders according to each tradition's own requirements.
outlook: Faith communities play a large role in Nigerian life, and chaplaincy roles also exist in schools, hospitals and the armed forces.

name: Professional Athlete / Sports Coach
summary: Athletes compete in sports, and coaches train them to perform at their best.
description: Professional athletes compete in sports such as football, athletics, basketball and boxing, while coaches plan training, develop skills and guide teams. In Nigeria they work with clubs, schools, state sports councils, academies and national teams, and many athletes play professionally abroad.
dayToDay: An athlete trains, recovers, studies tactics and competes; a coach plans sessions, analyses performance and supports players' development.
otherRoutes: Sports academies, school and club teams, and coaching certificates, including courses at the National Institute for Sports, Lagos.
outlook: Very few athletes reach the top, and careers are short, so it is wise to continue education and plan a second career such as coaching or sports management.

name: Sports Scientist / Fitness Trainer
summary: Sports scientists and fitness trainers use science to help people get fitter and perform better.
description: Sports scientists study how the body responds to exercise and help athletes improve performance and avoid injury, while fitness trainers coach individuals and groups to become healthier. They work with sports teams, gyms, schools, hospitals and wellness centres, or run their own fitness businesses.
dayToDay: A sports scientist tests athletes' fitness and designs training plans; a fitness trainer leads workouts and tracks clients' progress.
skills: Knowledge of the body and exercise
otherRoutes: Fitness instructor and personal trainer certificates are common routes into gym work.
outlook: Interest in fitness and sport is growing, creating opportunities in clubs, gyms and wellness businesses.
